div.head: TRINIDAD DURAZO.
div.p: Foregoing was followed by the affidavit of citizen Durazo, who, being subpoenaed, appeared before this court, and being duly sworn, stated that he is named as aforesaid; is thirty years of age; married; stock-raiser; native of the town of Granados, and at present resides at Nacozari. Being examined as to the statements in the communication of the commissary (of police) of Nacozari concerning him, the same being read to him, he testified that they are true; that on the 17th of last December an American force under command of Capt. Emmet Crawford, composed of 40 packers and 100 so-called tame Chiricahua Indians, passed through Nacozari; and that during their passage they fired upon the cattle which they encountered, without being restrained by the American officers commanding them; that after a little while he went out to learn what depredations had been committed, and that he found 4 head of cattle killed and 4 wounded; that two of these were the property of José M. Torres (1 killed and 1 wounded); 2 killed and 2 wounded belonged to his sister, Mrs. Apo Ionia Durazo de Langstone; 1 steer (two or three years old) belonged to Lorenzo Torres, and was wounded; and 1 cow belonging to himself was killed; that he has not the slightest doubt that said Indians committed those depredations, as they were seen in the act; that the American force left Nacozari, going toward Capadéhuache. Further deponent saith not.
This testimony being read to him he declared it correct. He did not sign it, being unable to write.
